title: nazm.check-report/1
description: What one `nazm check --cache-report` did: which modules were checked, which were reused, and why the rest were not. One object on stdout. It reports on work, never on meaning — a program's diagnostics and its exit status are the same with the cache on, off, cold or warm.

root.description: How the source root was decided: named with `--source-root`, found as a `nazm.root` marker, declared by a package manifest `nazm.toml` (N46), or derived from the file named on the command line. Only the first three make a module's identity independent of which file a compilation started from.

checked.description: Modules whose bodies were checked. `modules` minus `reused`.

reused.description: Modules whose bodies were not checked, because a valid entry recorded the same inputs. Zero with `--no-cache`.

missed.description: Checked because nothing was filed under their key.

rejected.description: Checked because what was filed could not be used: damaged, from another compiler, or an entry for something else. Never an error — a cache is derived data.

declined.description: Checked because the module has no durable identity to file anything under: outside the source root, or given two names by a symbolic link.

stored.description: Entries written this run. A module that produced any diagnostic writes none.
